user.title: Levoit ESPHome
user.description: Finds every ESPHome device that runs the levoit or philips component, links it to its config in the ESPHome Device Builder, and offers an update when its channel (stable or main) has a newer component version. Updates compile and upload through the Device Builder.

user.title: Add device
user.description: Make an ESPHome Device Builder config from a tuct/levoit template.

menu_options.existing: Device already in Home Assistant, without a config

existing.title: Existing device
existing.description: Its config gets the device's own name, and its API encryption key taken from Home Assistant's ESPHome connection to the device, so Home Assistant keeps the device.

variant.title: {model}
variant.description: Which ESP runs the device? A template config follows tuct/levoit: every update rewrites it from the newest template. Pick Other ESP for a board or pins without a template: that config is your own and is never rewritten.

custom.title: {model}: your own ESP
custom.description: A custom config, made from the {base} config of tuct/levoit with your board and UART pins. Updates never rewrite it; they only build the newer component it pulls.

data_description.board: ESPHome board name, e.g. seeed_xiao_esp32s3, esp32dev or esp32-c6-devkitc-1. Pick one or type another.
data_description.rx_pin: The ESP pin wired to the MCU's TX, e.g. GPIO5.
data_description.tx_pin: The ESP pin wired to the MCU's RX, e.g. GPIO4.

details.title: {model}
details.description: A new API encryption key and OTA password are generated and stored in the Device Builder's secrets.yaml under the device's name, e.g. levoit_everest_air_c3_api_key and levoit_everest_air_c3_ota_password. Wi-Fi comes from its wifi_ssid / wifi_password / wifi_ap_password secrets.

data_description.name: ESPHome name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
data_description.channel: Stable gets releases, main every merge.

details_existing.title: {model}: {name}
details_existing.description: The device keeps its name. Its API encryption key is taken from Home Assistant's ESPHome connection to the device (no key there: no encryption) and stored in the Device Builder's secrets.yaml as {api_secret}. Home Assistant does not know the OTA password: enter it if the device has one, leave it empty if not.

error.invalid_name: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 31 characters.

error.invalid_pin: Enter a GPIO number, e.g. GPIO5.
error.same_pin: RX and TX must be different pins.
error.name_taken: A device or config with this name exists already.
error.missing_wifi_secrets: The Device Builder's secrets.yaml has no {missing}. Add them there (Secrets in the Device Builder), then try again.
error.secret_exists: secrets.yaml already has {secret}. Remove it there or pick another name.
error.config_exists: The Device Builder already has a config with this name.
error.template_failed: The template could not be read from GitHub or does not have the expected shape.
error.cannot_connect: The ESPHome Device Builder did not answer.

create_entry.default: Config {configuration} created in the [ESPHome Device Builder]({builder_url}). Next: open the Device Builder, find {configuration}, choose Install, then Plug into this computer, and flash it once over USB. Until then it is listed as Not flashed yet on the Levoit ESPHome sidebar page. Once it is flashed and on your Wi-Fi it is added to the ESPHome integration automatically, and later updates come over the air from Home Assistant.
create_entry.existing: Config {configuration} created in the [ESPHome Device Builder]({builder_url}) for {name}, with its own name and keys. The next update installs it over the air.
